speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of the headache and exactly how your vision has changed over the last three weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any jaw pain or fatigue when chewing, and have you noticed any scalp tenderness, particularly when brushing your hair?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and symptoms, I am concerned about giant cell arteritis. REQUEST TEST: ESR and CRP levels to check for inflammation.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal inflammatory markers, giant cell arteritis is unlikely, so I need to rule out other causes of headache and vision loss. Do you have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or glaucoma, and have you noticed any visual field defects like a curtain coming down over your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you experience any visual auras, such as flashing lights or zigzag lines, before the headaches begin?

REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI and inflammatory markers are normal, I need to evaluate the eyes directly to distinguish between optic neuropathy and retinal issues. Have you noticed any pain when moving your eyes, and have you had a recent formal eye exam to check for glaucoma or macular degeneration? REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmology_consultation

text: The findings suggest a vascular etiology rather than inflammation or a mass. Given your history of hypertension and high cholesterol, do you experience any floaters or a sudden loss of vision in one eye, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs? REQUEST TEST: Carotid_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal carotid ultrasound rules out significant stenosis as the cause of your retinal vein occlusion. Given your hypertension and high cholesterol, I suspect a hypercoagulable state or local vascular risk factors are driving this issue. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_panel and Lipid_panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard coagulation and lipid panels are normal, I need to investigate less common thrombophilias or local vascular pathologies. REQUEST TEST: Hypercoagulability_screen and Orbital_CT_angiography

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive vision loss, headache, and retinal findings with normal systemic workup points to a local vascular event. DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
